newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr slips below 118 yen on MOF minister comments.
newsitem.headline: Dlr slips below 118 yen on MOF minister comments.

text.p: *Dollar quickly fell below 118 yen in reaction to Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka's comments on currency markets.
*He told news conference current weakness of yen is overdone and Japan will take proper steps against excessive currency movements.
*Long liquidation sales prompted falls of dollar against yen to near 117.60 yen, dealers said.
*But importers and Japanese institutional investors willing to buy on dips, which could support dollar near 117.50 yen, they added.
*On foreign exchange, Mitsuzuka said: "The recent weak trend of the yen is excessive. We will keep sufficient watch on currency moves and will act properly against wild currency moves."

*Asked if ministry sees need to come up with new measures to deal with falling stock prices other than early passage of extra budget for current fiscal year, Mitsuzuka said: "The ministry is keeping close watch on stock price moves with deep interest."
*He added: "As I have said, we will continue to make utmost efforts regarding the management of macroeconomic policies."

*Dollar bit easier against yen in mid-morning Tokyo, with topside heavy near 118.20 yen with profit-taking and wariness over possible dollar sales intervention by Japanese monetary authorities, dealers said.
*Market focusing on Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Senate Banking Committee later in day.
*Position-adjustment dominated dollar/mark trade, as profit-taking weighing on dollar's topside after dollar rose as high as 1.6312 markes overnight, dealers said.
